description: Create and start ONE new temporary process. Shows in DevGlow's AI Processes section. User can later [keep] or [dismiss] it. A name already used by another AI process stops and replaces that process. Before calling this, run list_projects: if the user already registered a project inside this checkout, call start_project instead so you run THEIR command, not a new one. Only use run_process when no matching project exists. In a git worktree of a registered project, this IS the right call: a project registered for the main checkout would run there, not in your worktree. Detect a worktree with `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir` (the two differ only in a linked worktree), reuse the project's command, port and interactive flag from get_project, set path to the matching directory in the worktree, and name it '<project name> (<branch>)'. If you are starting more than one process, call workspace_run once instead of calling this repeatedly — otherwise each process waits in the sidebar and the user sees nothing happen.

description.description: What the app does, plus any notes worth keeping (max 1000 chars). Helps the user remember the project later. Start with 1-2 plain sentences from the user's perspective; append findings or gotchas below if they ask.

interactive.description: Run in a PTY (interactive terminal) so tty-driven tools like `flutter run` / `expo start` enter interactive mode and accept key input (hot reload r, restart R). DEFAULT: omit — the command is auto-detected (flutter run, expo start, metro, react-native start ⇒ on). Only set explicitly to override that detection (true to force on, false to force plain pipe).

name.description: Display name for the process. Do NOT include port number in the name — use the port parameter instead.

port.description: Port number the process will listen on. Check package.json scripts or config files for --port flags. Important for DevGlow to show the correct port badge.

name: run_process

id.description: AI process id, for get_logs, stop_project and delete_process.

last_exit_reason.description: Last log line before it exited, when it exited right after start.

persisted.description: Whether DevGlow registered the process within the wait. false: do not rely on the id.

port_conflict.description: Set when the port was already taken; the process was registered but not started.

state.description: running: up. error: registered but not running (port conflict, or it exited right after start). pending: registered, not confirmed running yet. unknown: DevGlow had not registered it when the wait ran out, so do not rely on the id.

title: Run a new AI process
